FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: balut
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a duck egg incubated eighteen days, boiled and eaten in its own shell. You drink the broth first through the narrow end, then salt it and eat the rest. Sold in the evening, in the Philippines, to the cry of the seller.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: adobong balut
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: baluts shelled and then stewed in an adobo of {1_adj}, vinegar, {2_adj} and bay, until the sauce coats them.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: fried balut
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: baluts shelled, coated in an orange {1_adj} batter and fried in {2_plur}. The shell crisps, and the inside stays running.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: hột vịt lộn xào me
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: incubated eggs fried in a sweet-and-sour tamarind sauce, with crushed {1_coll} and {2_coll}. Eaten with rau răm leaves, whose bitterness cuts the fat.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pong tia koon
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the Cambodian version, grilled over embers rather than boiled, served with a dip of {1_adj}, salt and Kampot pepper.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: century egg
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} buried for weeks in an alkaline mixture of ash, lime and salt: the white turns to a translucent amber jelly, the yolk to a creamy green-black heart. Served in quarters with pickled {2_plur}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tea eggs
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: hard-boiled {0_coll} whose shells are cracked but never taken off, then stewed for hours in black {1_coll}, {2_coll} and star anise. The liquid seeps in through the cracks and draws a brown marbling.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: egg foo young
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a thick omelette loaded with {1_adj} and sprouts, fried into a domed cake and drowned in a brown {2_adj} sauce. Born in Chinese-American kitchens, and never carried back to China.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: beef carpaccio
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} stiffened in the cold then sliced to the edge of transparency, dressed with oil and {2_adj}, covered with shavings of {1_adj}. Invented in Venice for a countess who had been forbidden cooked meat.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sashimi
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} raw and sliced in one drawn stroke, never sawn, on a bed of shredded radish. The knife and the angle of the cut make the whole dish; there is nothing else to be done.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: crudo
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} raw in fine slivers, {1_adj} oil, flaked salt and the zest of {2_adj}. The Italian version of raw fish: no marinade, only a seasoning at the last moment.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tiradito
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} sliced the Japanese way but seasoned the Peruvian way: a yellow {1_adj} and {2_adj} sauce poured over just before serving, with no onion and no steeping.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: kitfo
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} chopped by knife and worked while still warm into a niter kibbeh — clarified butter with spices — with {2_adj} mitmita. Served raw, or barely warmed if you ask for it leb leb.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gored gored
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} raw in cubes rather than chopped, rolled in a spiced butter and awaze. The kitfo's cousin in pieces, and the most merciless test of freshness there is.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: mett
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} raw and minced the same day, salted and peppered, spread on bread with raw {1_coll} in rounds. Sold in the morning and never kept until evening.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the eggs of {1_adj} teased out of their sac in warm water, marinated in soy and sake, served heaped over rice belted with {2_plur}. They burst one by one under the tongue.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: twisted meat stew
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} braised very long in {1_plur} and {2_plur}: it is a tough flesh, and nothing shorter will tenderise it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: roast twisted meat
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a joint of {0_adj} barded with {1_plur} and stuck with {2_plur}, roasted under a lid. It gives up little juice and needs basting often.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: twisted meat skewers
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: cubes of {0_adj} marinated in {1_plur} and {2_plur}, threaded and grilled over a high flame. The marinade covers most of what there is to cover.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: twisted meat sausage
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} minced twice, let down with crumb and heavily {2_plur}, cased and then poached. The mincer settles the question of texture.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} braised in advance and shut under a {2_adj} pastry. What is under the crust can no longer be seen, and that is part of the point.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} stewed in a {1_adj} milk and a {2_adj} paste. The spices hold well on this flesh, which takes up more of them than is usual.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: strips of {0_adj} marinated in {2_plur} and {1_plur}, dried at a low temperature until they turn brittle. It keeps a long time, which was the only question.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: twisted meatballs
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} minced and bound with {1_plur}, rolled and finished in a {2_adj} sauce. The round shape recalls nothing in particular, and that is deliberate.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: twisted meat soup
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and its bones set in cold water and brought up gently, with {1_coll}. It is skimmed a great deal through the first hour.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: soda-glazed pork
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a ham cooked slowly in sweetened {0_coll}, whose sugar caramelises and whose acid tenderises. A recipe out of a tin-can kitchen, and nobody has ever explained why it works.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: lemonade sorbet
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} churned with pressed {2_coll} and a {1_adj} syrup, into a grainy, biting ice. The simplest dessert of a colony with no cow.
